In [[abstract algebra]], a '''basic subgroup''' is a [[subgroup]] of an [[abelian group]] which is a [[direct sum]] of [[cyclic group|cyclic subgroups]] and satisfies further technical conditions. This notion was introduced by L. Ya. Kulikov (for [[p-group|''p''-groups]]) and by László Fuchs (in general) in an attempt to formulate classification theory of infinite abelian groups that goes beyond the [[Prüfer theorems]]. It helps to reduce the classification problem to classification of possible [[group extension|extensions]] between two well understood classes of abelian groups: direct sums of cyclic groups and [[divisible group]]s.

== Definition and properties ==

A [[subgroup]], {{math|''B''}}, of an [[abelian group]], {{math|''A''}}, is called ''' ''p''-basic''', for a fixed [[prime number]], {{math|''p''}}, if the following conditions hold:

# {{math|''B''}} is a direct sum of [[cyclic group]]s of order {{math|''p{{sup|n}}''}} and infinite cyclic groups;
# {{math|''B''}} is a ''p''-[[pure subgroup]] of {{math|''A''}};
# The quotient group, {{math|''A''/''B''}}, is a ''p''-[[divisible group]].

Conditions 1–3 imply that the subgroup, {{math|''B''}}, is [[Hausdorff topological space|Hausdorff]] in the ''p''-adic topology of {{math|''B''}}, which moreover coincides with the topology [[induced topology|induced]] from {{math|''A''}}, and that {{math|''B''}} is [[dense subset|dense]] in {{math|''A''}}. Picking a generator in each cyclic direct summand of {{math|''B''}} creates a '' ''p''-basis'' of ''B'', which is analogous to a [[basis (linear algebra)|basis]] of a [[vector space]] or a [[free abelian group]].

Every abelian group, {{math|''A''}}, contains ''p''-basic subgroups for each {{math|''p''}}, and any 2 ''p''-basic subgroups of {{math|''A''}} are isomorphic. Abelian groups that contain a unique ''p''-basic subgroup have been completely characterized. For the case of [[p-group|''p''-groups]] they are either [[divisible group|divisible]] or ''bounded''; i.e., have bounded exponent. In general, the isomorphism class of the quotient, {{math|''A''/''B''}} by a basic subgroup, {{math|''B''}}, may depend on {{math|''B''}}.
